character_facts: The Baron suffers catastrophic injuries to his groin and hips but survives.
The Baron remains bedridden for months and is mentally distressed during recovery.
Shazam is associated with the Baron's survival and return journey.
Iku-Tta and his daughters personally tend to the Baron's care.
The Baron's son is described as destined to become a renowned warrior.
characters_present: an elderly bedside attendant or speaker (possibly Iku-Tta)
continuity_links: This page follows an earlier event in which the Baron was mutilated in the groin and hips.
It refers back to a prior incident involving the death of someone the Baron fears may have been his son.
It sets up the future importance of the Baron's son as a warrior.
dialogue_meaning: Narration states that the Baron's groin and hips were destroyed and that Shazam enabled his return to the palace.
Narration states that Iku-Tta and his two daughters nursed the Baron through a recovery lasting several months.
The Baron, apparently delirious, insists he killed a pirate rather than his son and calls for Bari to return.
The bedside speaker comforts him with a symbolic story about a rare scarlet bird becoming a flower that grows upward.
The speaker foretells that the Baron's son will become a famous warrior and urges the Baron to rest.
locations: an outdoor night landscape during the Baron's return
the Baron's sickbed or recovery chamber
lore_facts: Shazam is capable of bringing the severely wounded Baron back to his palace.
Iku-Tta is loyal to the Baron.
The Baron's palace serves as a place of recovery after catastrophic injury.
Prophetic or symbolic speech is used to speak about the fate of the Baron's son.
plot_events: The Baron is shown grievously injured, especially in the groin and hips.
He survives long enough to return to his palace with Shazam's help.
He spends several months near death while recovering.
Iku-Tta and his two daughters care for him during his recovery.
While bedridden, the Baron cries out about killing a pirate rather than his son and calls for 'Bari' to answer.
A bedside figure tries to soothe him and predicts that his son will become a renowned warrior.
uncertainties: Some dialogue is difficult to read precisely; 'Bari' may be slightly misread.
The exact identity of the bedside speaker is not fully certain from this page alone.
The exact visual status of Shazam in the middle panels is somewhat ambiguous due to the stylized, spectral rendering.
visual_summary: The page shows the badly wounded Baron clutching his lower body in armor, then a night escape associated with his mount Shazam, including a ghostly horse image and a ride through a pale, wild landscape. In the final large panel, the Baron lies bandaged in bed near a fire while Iku-Tta and two daughters tend him; he appears feverish or delirious as another figure speaks to calm him.
